task.title: Simplify the AWKIT Claude Code workflow to a single-agent default
task.objective: Make one capable primary agent complete one normal task end to end. Change the orchestration DEFAULT from delegation to single-agent execution, make every subagent invocation explicit and conditional on a named trigger, prohibit recursive delegation and automatic external-model delegation, and separate routine context from historical context. Remove duplicate reasoning, not engineering validation: no check is deleted, no activation rule is weakened, no security control is relaxed.

acceptance.description: The orchestration default is single-agent execution. CONCURRENCY_POLICY.defaultMode is no longer "subagents", and the generated agent definitions state that a routed role is performed by the primary agent unless a named escalation trigger fires.

Every subagent invocation is gated on an explicit trigger list. Routine work (Risk 0-1, single layer, no risk flag) delegates to nobody; review delegation requires a major-phase, security, concurrency, persistence-migration, architectural or explicitly-requested trigger.

No activation rule, risk level, path ownership, evidence vocabulary or verifier assertion is removed or relaxed. verify:agent-routing passes with its unconditional-check count unchanged at 1036, proving no assertion stopped running.
Subagents complete their own scope and cannot spawn further agents; this remains enforced in code and is now stated in the written policy.
glm-delegate is never invoked automatically; the policy names the only three conditions under which it may be used and forbids routine search, summary, formatting, test execution and state updates.
Routine task context is an explicitly named short list; historical and archival documents are on-demand only and do not auto-load.
All 18 generated platform files match the registry byte-for-byte after regeneration, so no second source of truth is introduced.

evidence.notes: Ran; exits 1 with 1039/1040 passed, 1040 run. RED ON ARRIVAL: the identical two failures and the identical cardinality were measured BEFORE any edit in this task, under a temporarily released lease. (1) 'the rendered matrix is byte-identical to the registry it derives from' - docs/ai/routing/ROUTING_MATRIX.md is UNMODIFIED in the working tree, so the committed file already disagreed with the registry, and its renderer tools/agents/render-docs.mjs does not import context-policy.mjs at all, which is the only module this task changed. (2) 'suite cardinality - expected 1037 assertions, ran 1040' is a RISE, not a DROP: three assertions were added by an earlier commit without the deliberate re-pin the guard's own message demands. A RISE means nothing stopped running. Not re-pinned here: re-pinning would erase the signal, and scripts/** is qa-owned and outside the manager lease. The acceptance clause this evidence serves - that no assertion stopped running - is PROVEN by the before/after equality, not by a green exit code.

Ran after regeneration: 'All generated agent definitions are current.' All 18 generated files (16 .claude/agents/*.md plus the Codex and Gemini agent-routing skills) are byte-identical to what the registry renders, so no second source of truth was introduced. Regenerated with the allowlisted exact form 'node tools/agents/render-platform-agents.mjs --write'; the npm alias agent:render-agents is not in the lease-guard shell allowlist.

Derived by inspection from the two authorities, read at their current state: ACTIVATION_RULES in tools/agents/routing-matrix.mjs (lines 1318-1434, UNCHANGED by this task) decides which roles are accountable; delegationDecisionFor() and specialistLimitFor() in tools/agents/context-policy.mjs decide how many of them are performed by a spawned subagent rather than by the primary agent. Executed as an inspection because the contract declared command: null, and because lease-guard.mjs refuses arbitrary 'node -e' by design - its shell allowlist is a closed explicit set, which is correct behavior and not a workaround target. The discriminator to read: routed role count is UNCHANGED in every scenario; only the subagent count moves. Scenarios 1-3 name no trigger and spawn nobody. Scenario 3b is the same persistence area with migration_required, and it crosses into delegation - which is the evidence that the gate is the named trigger, not the subject area.

scenarios.example: a button label misaligns in the renderer
scenarios.expected: The primary agent makes the design judgment (uiux), edits app/renderer/** (frontend) and runs the targeted check itself (qa). Four accountable roles, zero model requests beyond the primary.

scenarios.example: a scoped TypeScript product module with no narrower owner
scenarios.expected: Primary implements and validates end to end. This is the case the executive prompt names as the target topology.

scenarios.example: add an optional field to a persisted JSON shape, no migration
scenarios.expected: persistence remains accountable for unknown-field preservation and old-data compatibility; the primary discharges that role rather than spawning it. No check is skipped.

scenarios.example: the same area, but the shape change requires a migration
scenarios.expected: One independent reviewer, diff-first. Included deliberately as the control for scenario 3: same files, same owner, different answer - proving the gate is the named trigger and not the subject area.

scenarios.example: an IPC contract plus a concurrency change spanning renderer, main and runner
scenarios.expected: Two triggers named, so two independent readers are authorized, under a ceiling of 3 from specialistLimitFor(crossLayerCount >= 2). Still below the ceiling: parallel reviewers of one diff mostly re-derive each other.

scenarios.example: packaging and offline-boundary changes at a release candidate
scenarios.expected: The one class where the ceiling itself binds: two triggers request two readers and routineSpecialists allows exactly two. Offline and packaging validation is unchanged and still runs.

policy_assertions_checked: external-delegation-opt-in: EXTERNAL_DELEGATION_POLICY.automatic === false in every scenario above; no scenario reaches glm-delegate, and neverFor explicitly excludes file searching, summaries, formatting, test execution, simple edits and project-state updates.
context-separation: CONTEXT_LOADING.routine is a named 7-item list; CONTEXT_LOADING.historical (phase reports, historical audits, archived change requests) is on-demand only and does not auto-load.
no-recursive-delegation: NESTED_DELEGATION.allowedByDefault === false, so any subagent in scenarios 3b, 4 and 5 completes its own scope and cannot spawn further agents.

evidence.notes: Ran rather than assumed, which was the point of declaring it optional instead of NOT APPLICABLE: 'tsc --noEmit' clean and all three bundles built (main 1,542.27 kB, preload 20.57 kB, renderer 2,032.65 kB). Separately, 'npm run typecheck:scripts' FAILS on scripts/verify-write-queue.mts (TS7060, TS2345) - that file is UNMODIFIED in the working tree, and tsconfig.scripts.json includes only 'scripts/**/*.mts', so it does not cover the tools/agents/*.mjs files this task edited. Pre-existing and out of scope, recorded here rather than omitted.

acceptance_verdicts.single-agent-default: MET. CONCURRENCY_POLICY.defaultMode is 'single-agent'; all 18 generated definitions carry a 'How this role is performed' section and agent-render-check is PASS.
acceptance_verdicts.conditional-delegation: MET. delegationDecisionFor() returns delegate:false with maxSubagents:0 unless a trigger from DELEGATION_TRIGGERS is NAMED; scenarios 1-3 spawn nobody and 3b/4/5 are gated on named triggers.
acceptance_verdicts.no-weakened-checks: MET IN SUBSTANCE, NOT AS LITERALLY WORDED. The clause 'verify:agent-routing passes' is NOT satisfied - the gate exits 1. It also exited 1, with the identical failure set and identical cardinality (1039/1040 passed, 1040 run), BEFORE any edit in this task. The operative claim - that no activation rule, risk level, path ownership, evidence vocabulary or verifier assertion was removed or relaxed, and that no assertion stopped running - is proven by that before/after equality. The wording assumed a green gate on arrival; it was red. Recorded as a shortfall in the criterion I wrote, not as a pass.
acceptance_verdicts.no-recursive-delegation: MET. NESTED_DELEGATION.allowedByDefault === false and requiresExplicitPrimaryAuthorization === true, now stated in CLAUDE.md and in every generated definition.
acceptance_verdicts.external-delegation-opt-in: MET. EXTERNAL_DELEGATION_POLICY.automatic === false, with three allowedWhen conditions and six neverFor exclusions.
acceptance_verdicts.context-separation: MET WITH A DECLARED DEVIATION. Implemented as CONTEXT_LOADING routine/onDemand/historical tiers over the existing docs/ai/ tree, NOT as the new .ai/project-state.md the executive prompt named. Creating a parallel .ai/ tree would have produced exactly the second source of truth that docs/ai/DECISIONS.md binds against, and verify:roadmap-dashboard already parses 13 of the existing files.
acceptance_verdicts.generated-files-consistent: MET. agent:check-agents PASS across all 18 files.

completion.notes: Closed. Evidence was declared before implementation, per the manager rule that evidence chosen afterwards tends to be evidence that passes - and that rule earned its keep here: the pre-declared agent-routing criterion caught that the governing gate was already red, which a criterion written afterwards would have quietly reworded. Three pre-existing failures were found and NOT fixed, all outside the manager lease and outside this task's scope: the ROUTING_MATRIX.md byte-identity drift (committed; remediation is one allowlisted command, 'node tools/agents/render-docs.mjs --write', deliberately not run because the manager does not own that file and regenerating could discard someone's intentional edit), the +3 suite cardinality rise, and the scripts/verify-write-queue.mts typecheck errors.
